beats.headline: Gear that will not change hands
beats.text: Most of what the hunters carry is restricted to the hunter. Florin took out two Goriffs, blue aliens with antennae like twin elephant trunks, and has their pulse rifles and electric armour, but he cannot equip them. Donut's sunglasses carry the same restriction, as Louis learned when he tried them on. Mordecai says it is a common addition to benefactor box items, to keep players from murdering the recipients for their gear. A rare scroll called Cracker Jack can free an item, but nobody they know has one. They collect everything anyway.

beats.headline: Three, for a bin
beats.text: Orren means to take a plastic bin of loot back from Carl, for its communicator and Valtay upgrade pills, while Quasar argues caselaw. Carl does not care. He offers to trade for the bin, and Orren warns that the AI's value on it may disappoint; Carl just wants to finish the floor. For the homeless man's dirty clothes and a few Valtay items he receives a single wand recharge scroll, three scrolls called Cracker Jack, and leave to keep the four cretins for the ninth floor. Orren will not give back the Gate of the Feral Gods.

beats.headline: Two shields unlocked
beats.text: Carl spends two of the three Cracker Jack scrolls on a pair of alien shields from the pile of tech looted from hunters, unusable until unlocked. His is a Valtay Perso-Shield, Platinum Edition, a pinback button like the planet Saturn, identical to the one he would have had from Paulie. Donut's is the Bull Rush, a longhorn pin from Hereford War Machines. Neither has been tested in a real fight yet.

beats.headline: Not for the guns
beats.text: Most of the guns they have looted are user locked, and unlocking one would waste a precious Cracker Jack scroll. The bigger guns carry no such restriction, so those sit in the fortified bunkers along the line, made of a composite concrete different from the castle's and almost impenetrable, while the earthworks teams work underfoot.
